records.place: Upper Moutere, the Moutere Hills, Nelson

wine.name: Neudorf Home Block Moutere Chardonnay
wine.grapes: Chardonnay alone, built on the Mendoza clone, which the house credits with the wine's firm acid and high extract.
wine.sites: The Home Block at Upper Moutere, planted in 1978 and by the house's account among the oldest commercial Chardonnay vineyards of the South Island, farmed organically and without irrigation for more than four decades on the clay gravels of the Moutere Hills.
wine.making: Fermented wholly in French oak barrels with wild yeast and a high share of solids, about a sixth of the oak new in the 2022 to 2024 vintages. The wine rests for some ten months on its full lees, stirred each month until the malolactic fermentation is done, then for a few months more on fine lees in stainless steel before bottling.
wine.glass: Lemon curd, white peach and lily over a note of home baking and pie crust, with a seam of oyster shell; firm acidity from the Mendoza clone and a fine, layered texture from the lees.
wine.ageing: Open on release, it develops slowly in bottle; five to ten years suit most vintages, and older bottles have held well past a decade.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle briefly if it seems tight; a wide white wine or Burgundy glass.

records.table: Planted at Upper Moutere in 1978 and never irrigated, the vines of Neudorf's Home Block Moutere Chardonnay grow on clay gravels and are farmed organically. Wild fermented in barrel and raised on its lees, it gives lemon curd, white peach and pie crust over firm acidity.
records.story: In 1976 a young couple moved into the Moutere Hills, buying a former commune property, three years after the Seifried family had planted the first modern vineyard of the region at Upper Moutere. In 1978 they planted their first vines there, Chardonnay among them, on the weathered clay gravels of the hills. That planting, the Home Block, is by the house's account among the oldest commercial Chardonnay vineyards of the South Island, and it rests on the Mendoza clone, which the house credits with the firm acid and high extract of its wine. The vines have never been irrigated, a rule the estate has kept for more than four decades, and the vineyards came to be farmed organically. For years the wine was sold simply as Moutere Chardonnay; the label later named the Home Block it comes from, and a second Chardonnay joined it from Rosie's Block, bought in 1999 and made the same way so that each site can speak. Pinot Noir and Riesling from the same hills complete the range. The Home Block wine carried the name of Nelson's clay hills into New Zealand Chardonnay, and it is the wine to taste for what the Moutere gives.

wine.name: Seifried Winemakers Collection Sweet Agnes Riesling
wine.sites: In the vintages the house describes, the Edens Road vineyard, bordered by the Wairoa River, on markedly stony soil; the house picks from whichever of its estate vineyards gives the ripest fruit that year.
wine.making: Picked late and by hand, without botrytis, from grapes much of which have shrivelled and raisined on the vine by natural drying. The berries are pressed gently, and the concentrated juice ferments for some two and a half to three weeks before the young wine is stabilised and bottled early, within months of the harvest. It is not made in every year: none was made in 2020.
wine.glass: Apricot, honey and crystallised citrus peel, with orange marmalade in some years; very sweet and luscious, held in balance by tangy Riesling acidity.
wine.ageing: Delicious young for its fruit, it keeps its acidity well in bottle and gains a deeper, honeyed character with age.
wine.serve: 6 to 8 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a small white wine glass and a modest pour, with blue cheese or a fruit tart.

records.table: Grapes raisined on the vine without botrytis, picked late by hand, make Seifried Estate's Sweet Agnes Riesling, named for the co-founder: apricot, honey and candied peel over tangy acidity. Pour it cold, in a small glass.
records.story: An Austrian born winemaker came to Nelson in 1971 to make apple wine for the New Zealand Apple and Pear Board, and there met his future wife, who had grown up on a Southland sheep farm. Together they bought land in the Moutere valley and in 1973 planted the first modern vineyard of the region, at a time when many, government farm advisers among them, held the South Island unsuitable for wine. Their first vintage followed in 1976, sold from the cellar door at Upper Moutere. The family kept planting: the Redwood Valley vineyard, a north facing slope on solid Moutere clay, went in in 1979 by the family's account, and later sites spread across the Waimea Plains. In 1998 the first vineyard of 1973 passed to new owners as Kahurangi Estate. Sweet Agnes, named for the co-founder, became the family's sweet Riesling, made only when the late autumn lets the grapes shrivel and concentrate on the vine without rot. In 2014 the Decanter World Wine Awards gave its 2012 vintage a regional trophy for New Zealand sweet wine. In one glass it holds the founding family's way with Riesling and a New World sweet wine made from raisined rather than botrytised grapes.

wine.name: Greenhough Hope Vineyard Pinot Noir
wine.grapes: Pinot Noir alone, built by the house's account on its oldest vines, of the clones UCD5 and AM 10/5, planted in 1993.
wine.sites: The home vineyard at Hope, inland on the Waimea Plains: clay rich loam and river stones over deep gravels laid down by the Wairoa River, the clay holding moisture; certified organic since 2011.
wine.making: Picked by hand and destemmed into small open fermenters, a share fermented as whole bunches in the vintages of the 2020s, which the house says has only lately joined the style. Raised for about ten months to a year in French oak barriques, a small part new. Fining and filtering have changed: the 2014 was fined with egg white and filtered, the 2023 bottled unfined and lightly filtered.
wine.glass: Sliced strawberry and orange peel over a savoury edge and a spicy perfume; fragrant and elegantly built, medium bodied, with a dry, appetising backbone.
wine.ageing: Fragrant on release, it may close for a spell in its first years and opens again with more time in bottle; most vintages drink well within a decade.
wine.serve: 13 to 15 degrees Celsius; no need to decant, though a young bottle opens with half an hour of air; a Burgundy glass.

records.table: On clay loam over river gravels at Hope, the family's organic home vineyard gives Greenhough's Hope Vineyard Pinot Noir. Made in small open fermenters, lately with a share of whole bunches, it is fragrant and savoury, with strawberry, orange peel and a dry backbone.
records.story: The gravels of Hope were laid down some twenty thousand years ago, as the house tells it, when frost broke the eastern ranges and the floods of the Wairoa River spread loose stones across the plain; a finer clay loam in the upper soil sets this inland site apart from the stonier terraces nearer the sea. In late 1990 a young couple left Auckland for this rural pocket of Nelson and took on an established vineyard, and their family estate took its name from them. Their oldest vines, the clones UCD5 and AM 10/5, went in in 1993 and became the core of the Hope Vineyard Pinot Noir, with a barrel fermented Chardonnay and a sweeter styled Riesling beside it. In 2008 the couple turned the home vineyard over to organic farming, and after the three year conversion it was certified by BioGro, the New Zealand organic body, in 2011. In the vintages of the 2020s a share of the Pinot Noir has been fermented as whole bunches, and the latest are bottled unfined. Against the Pinot Noir of the Moutere Hills it is the Waimea Plains' reply: a small, family made, organic red from the flat land near the city, fragrant and savoury rather than weighty.

wine.name: Kahurangi Estate Riesling
wine.sites: The home block near Upper Moutere village, first planted in 1973 by the Seifried family, whose Riesling vines the house describes as the oldest commercial Riesling of the South Island.
wine.making: The house publishes little of its cellar method for this wine. It is a single vineyard wine from the old vines of the home block, made in a dry or nearly dry style, with the touch of sweetness set by the vintage.
wine.glass: Lemon, lime and a flinty note on the nose, then grapefruit and green apple on the palate, with juicy acidity and a long finish; age brings a fuller, more complex texture.
wine.ageing: Fresh and citrus led when young, it gains texture and complexity with several years in bottle.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a white wine glass, with smoked fish or a light seafood dish.

records.story: The first vineyard at Upper Moutere is where the modern wine of Nelson began. In 1973 the Seifried family planted the region's first modern vines here, on the clay soils of the Moutere Hills, and made its first vintage from them in 1976. As the Seifrieds planted elsewhere, the original site changed hands: in 1998 a new family bought it and renamed it Kahurangi Estate. Its claim to note is its Riesling, which the house describes as the oldest commercial Riesling vines of the South Island. That claim is the house's and its stockists', and it is shared: the couple who founded Kahurangi Estate also founded Heaphy, whose winery stands on Sunrise Road at Upper Moutere and whose old vine Riesling comes from blocks the Seifried family planted in the early 1970s, so the wine is safer told as Riesling from the vines of 1973. The house bottles a single vineyard Nelson Riesling and a Mt Arthur Reserve Riesling, and its range runs on to Estate Reserve and Regional Selection wines. Half a century of Moutere Riesling vines speak in it: a lean, citrus led white with real length.

wine.name: Rimu Grove Pinot Noir
wine.grapes: Pinot Noir alone, from several clones grown on the estate.
wine.sites: The estate vineyard, planted in 1995 on a gentle north facing slope of the Bronte Peninsula, overlooking the Waimea Inlet, on clay and gravel soils of the Moutere.
wine.making: Picked by hand and cold soaked for five to seven days before fermenting in small open vats, plunged by hand three times a day. The wine is aged in French oak barrels, for about ten months in some vintages and nearly two years in others, and bottled unfiltered in some vintages and coarse filtered in others.
wine.glass: Dark plum and sweet berry over bramble, mushroom and savoury spice; smooth and full, with juicy acidity, fine grained tannin and a long, graceful finish.
wine.ageing: Approachable within a few years of the vintage; the house has offered library vintages going back two decades, and age draws out its mushroom notes.
wine.serve: 14 to 16 degrees Celsius; no need to decant a young bottle, an old one gently off its sediment; a Burgundy glass.

records.table: A small winery planted in 1995 on a north facing slope above the Waimea Inlet makes Rimu Grove Pinot Noir, its estate red. Cold soaked and plunged by hand in small open vats, it gives plum, bramble and mushroom over fine grained tannin.
records.story: The vineyard of Rimu Grove lies on the Bronte Peninsula, a finger of the Moutere coast reaching into the Waimea Inlet west of Nelson city, on a gentle north facing slope. In 1995 its founder, a Californian, bought the site and planted it with Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris, making Pinot Noir the focus of the house. The estate Pinot Noir is made in the Burgundian manner: hand picked, cold soaked, fermented in small open vats plunged by hand, aged in French oak and bottled with little or no filtration. The first Rimu Grove wine followed in 2000. With the years the range grew around it: Bronte wines from the peninsula, a Pinot Noir called Synergy, and Pinot Noirs named for Mapua and for the view, while the winery's own bar became a place to taste them. Rimu Grove has also kept back older vintages, and its lists have offered Pinot Noir going back to the 2000 vintage, a rare chance to taste aged Nelson red. Pour it as the coastal Moutere's Pinot Noir beside the Chardonnay of the hills: a small, single estate wine whose savoury notes are the Moutere clay's gift to Pinot Noir with age.

cards.front: Rimu Grove Pinot Noir: how long are the grapes cold soaked before fermenting?
cards.back: Five to seven days, before fermenting in small open vats plunged by hand.

questions.q: A guest asks how the Rimu Grove Pinot Noir is fermented. Which answer fits?
opts: In small open vats, plunged by hand
In large closed steel tanks, pumped over
By carbonic maceration in sealed vats
In clay amphora buried in the vineyard
questions.exp: The house cold soaks the hand picked grapes and ferments them in small open vats plunged by hand several times a day; nothing points to carbonic maceration or amphora.

questions.q: The estate vineyard of Rimu Grove on the Bronte Peninsula was planted in which year?
questions.exp: The founder bought and planted the Bronte Peninsula site in 1995; 1973 and 1978 are the plantings of Seifried and Neudorf in the Moutere.

report: Swap proposed: Rimu Grove is a small estate whose recent face is a bar and restaurant, its sources are thin and mostly its own, and it is not in the region record; Waimea Estates or Mahana should be researched as a fifth house a guest is likelier to know.
Founded 1995 rests on Glengarry, Grape to Glass and the house's own vineyard page; the Taste Nelson timeline alone gives 1980 and is not followed.
The oak time runs from ten to twenty two months across the vintage pages, so the making gives a range and no figure for new oak.
The Bronte wine is called Bronte Pinot Noir on some pages and a blend of Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Meunier on a drinks menu; the trap tells only what the menu says.
The rimu as the source of the name is general knowledge, not a sourced claim of the house; cut it if the checker wants a source.
The founder may be living and is never named.

changed: wine.sites and story: the former orchard cut, no source.

wine.making: cold soak of five to seven days and plunging three times a day from the house's vintage notes; bottled without fining or filtration was wrong for some years: the 2004 and 2005 were coarse filtered.
table: bottled unfined replaced by cold soaked and plunged by hand.
story: the founder a Californian, and the first wine of 2000 (Taste Nelson, Top Tastes, the house's back vintages).
